chapter_theme: Silent samadhi (மோன சமாதி): the state beyond posture, speech and the grades of the Lord's forms, given only by the guru and known only by having it, as a taste is known by eating or a wife's joy by the wife; in it self, mind and the knower dissolve, and the one who stands united sees the Supreme and the ages.
structure_note: Opening verses set the state beyond posture and book learning (2936, 2937); a run describes the Lord met there beyond turiya and beyond every named form (2939 to 2943); three verses argue that the experience can't be told, by the images of marriage and the bitter fruit (2944 to 2946, with 2950); the chapter ends in first-person dissolution and union (2951 to 2953).

2936.reading: For those who have gone on there is no saying that they stood, sat or lay: their mind is silent samadhi; there is one hidden thing that dwells in the hall, and this is how those who went there and drew near join it.
2936.nuance: The first line denies the postures of the body: the state isn't a matter of how one sits. மன்று (the hall) is traditionally Siva's dance-hall at Chidambaram, taken also as the inner space; மறைப்பொருள் is a hidden or secret thing, or the meaning of the Veda (மறை).

2937.reading: What use is it to write down on the outside of a palm leaf that cause which lies beyond every sign that points and every mark? Unless guru Nandi joins one to it, it is like the hanging teat on a goat's neck.
2937.nuance: ஏட்டின் புறத்தில் is book learning, writing on the leaf's surface. The goat's-neck image, ஆட்டின் கழுத்தில் அதர், is usually taken as the fleshy tags under a goat's throat, which look like teats and give no milk: knowledge on the page looks like the real thing and feeds no one. அதர் for these tags is the traditional gloss.

2938.reading: To those who have awareness the world appears; to those who have awareness no sorrow comes; at the moment those who have awareness realised, they realised and saw.
2938.nuance: Every line opens with உணர்வுடையார், and the last two lines turn back on themselves, perhaps to say that realising and seeing are one act. உலகமும் தோன்றும் may mean the world is seen as it is, or that a further world (Siva's) shows itself; the verse doesn't settle which.

2939.reading: The good lord of the wondrous land, who stands as forgetting itself, the great gracious one free of birth, the glorious one, sleeps with the holy lady in an enjoyment that has no sleep.
2939.nuance: மறப்பது வாய்நின்ற may be the Lord as concealment, one of his five acts, or as the forgetting of the world in samadhi. மாய நன்னாடன் is the lord of maya's land or of a wondrous land. The last line is a paradox, a sleep that is no sleep, the tradition's name for the yogic sleep of union.

2940.reading: The light that shines beyond the three turiyas, and beyond the rare turiya above them as a third, swallowing and spitting out expansion and contraction, is within the experience beyond speech.
2940.nuance: துரியம் is the fourth state of consciousness; the three turiyas are traditionally the soul's, Shakti's and Siva's, but the count in lines 1 and 2 is hard to fix. விரிவு குவிவு (spreading and drawing in) may be the world's emanation and withdrawal or the mind's going out and coming back, as in 2981. உரையில் அநுபூதி is direct experience that words don't reach.

2941.reading: The formless one, without flesh, without any lack, without wealth, without evil, god of the gods, without equal, master of the army of goblins, the one who clings to nothing, came and entered my mind.
2941.nuance: A string of negatives in -இலி. திருவிலி is odd in praise: it may mean he needs no fortune or ornament, or that he is without Tiru (Lakshmi), unlike Vishnu. மருவிலி may be 'without attachment' or 'without mixture'. The ending turns the list of absences into a personal arrival.

2942.reading: No one has seen and known Nandi who is in the body, yet those of the eight directions praise him as the Lord; we do not know the ford where his servants scooped up the measureless bliss beyond the worlds.
2942.nuance: துறை is a bathing ghat or landing place, the way down to the water; முகந்த is scooping water in the hands. The speaker includes himself among those who don't know, perhaps in modesty, perhaps to say the way can't be shown.

2943.reading: He is not the Supreme, not Sadasiva, not the formless, not the state with form; becoming a wonder, like the desire of lovers in their enjoyment, he stands mingled without imagining.
2943.nuance: தற்பரம், சதாசிவன், நிட்களம் and சகளம் are the Siddhanta names for the grades of the Lord's being, formless to embodied; the verse denies each. அனுபோகக் காமம் போல் compares union to sexual joy known only in the act, an image the chapter repeats in 2944 and 2950. கற்பனை இன்றி may mean without mental construction on the knower's side.

2944.reading: Fools see with the eyes in their faces; seeing with the eye within is bliss; if a daughter says 'tell me', how can a mother tell her the joy she had with her husband?
2944.nuance: The marriage image makes the claim concrete: the bliss is real and private, and the one who has it can't hand it on in words, as the next verse but one also argues.

2945.reading: The Father joining like salt in water, leaving both the Parapara that is spoken of and the Supreme one reaches, the clinging word and its state dissolving in that mingling: as it is, so it is, that is the way.
2945.nuance: Salt dissolved in water is the classic image of union without remainder. பராபரம் and பரம் are grades of the Supreme. கப்புறு is obscure, perhaps 'branching' or 'clinging'; சொற்பதம் may be word and meaning or the levels of speech. எப்படி அப்படி, 'how, so', gives up description.

2946.reading: The nux vomica fruit is lovely to those who look at it, but its taste is known to those who eat it; when a girl has come to full womanhood and is a young wife, the man who took her knows her many qualities.
2946.nuance: காஞ்சிரம் is the strychnine tree, whose fruit is handsome and bitter. Both images say the same thing, that only the one who has it knows a thing's nature; the chapter applies this to samadhi. The first image may also warn that a pleasing look deceives.

2947.reading: Nandi sat in the middle street, and the junctions and the samadhis ceased of themselves; I joined, with my understanding, the light that rises and springs up within the navel.
2947.nuance: நடுவுத் தெரு is traditionally the central channel of the yogic body (sushumna); சந்தி may be the junctions of the breaths or of the day kept in sandhya worship. உந்தி (the navel) is a seat of fire in the body. The plain sense is that, once the Lord is at the centre, rites and practised samadhis fall away.

2948.reading: Staying apart without being shaken and examining, studying the ancient Veda without haste, he subsides into the void that shook off that imagining which passed beyond the void that cried out.
2948.nuance: கதறிய பாழ் (the void that cried out) and உதறிய பாழ் (the void that shook off) are obscure; they may be grades of the three voids of earlier chapters. The subject of ஒடுங்குகின்றான் may be the seeker or the Lord.

2949.reading: The red feet adorned with unfading flowers, which the gods do not reach: for those on the path of dharma to rejoice day by day, going within the bright flame in the full lotus, the nectar flows for those who seek, and it is the nectar the seekers seek.
2949.nuance: நாடார் can be 'those who seek' or 'those who do not seek', and the last line plays on both; it could also say the nectar is not for those who don't seek. சேடார் கமலம், the lotus full of petals, is traditionally a centre of the yogic body, often the crown. வானவர் கூடார் may also be read as the gods who gather.

2950.reading: As desire shows itself suddenly even on hearing the words of two who sat together for that purpose, so the Lord with the honeyed konrai garland gives his wealth, then and there, to look upon those who have suddenly made themselves ready apart.
2950.nuance: பொதுக்கென and சதுக்கென are sound-words for suddenness. The comparison is again sexual: desire is kindled at once by hearing of it, and grace comes as fast. அன்றே may be 'that very day' or an emphatic ending.

2951.reading: Self destroyed, wealth destroyed, the long-lasting flesh destroyed, life destroyed with it, the sky destroyed and the mind destroyed, I do not know that I too was destroyed.
2951.nuance: The list runs from outer to inner and ends in a paradox: the one who would know of his own undoing is gone. தான் and நான் may be distinguished, the self as agent and the knower. வான் may be the element space or the heavens.

2952.reading: Turning away both darkness and the open light, becoming the thing within the thing and fitted within, I stood with a stone-like mind that no longer rolls, joined to the feet of the Father by whose grace things are undone.
2952.nuance: இருளும் வெளியும் may be ignorance and knowledge, or the states of the soul alone and in the body. உருளாத கன்மனம் can be a mind fixed and steady, or the hard heart that would not melt, offered in humility. What அருளால் அழிந்திடும் destroys isn't said.

2953.reading: Standing united, I knew the Parapara within; standing united, I knew the way of Siva within; standing united, I knew awareness itself within; standing united, I have seen many ages.
2953.nuance: ஒன்றிநின்று (standing as one) opens every line. பல ஊழி கண்டேன் may be the timelessness of the state, or, in tradition, Tirumular's own long life in yoga.

links.note: Both make the highest state a kind of sleep: in 129 the wise saw Siva-bhoga within while sleeping; here the Lord and the lady sleep in an enjoyment that has no sleep.
Both use the same phrase for the hidden way in, the ford no one knows (துறை அறியோம், துறையறிவார் இல்லை): in 1987 the breath that circles and lies plugged, here the place where devotees drew bliss.

Two arguments for the same claim, that the state is known only by having it: the mother can't tell her daughter her joy, and the taste of the fruit and the nature of a wife are known only to the eater and the husband.

Both use spreading and drawing in (விரிவு குவிவு, விரிந்து குவிந்தது): here the light beyond turiya swallows and spits out the movement; in 2981 it is the mind's movement, whose end with speech is release.

The Kural promises a world above the gods to one who cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine'; Tirumular describes the cutting from inside, the self, wealth, body and mind undone until even the 'I' that would notice is gone.
